question: What kind of speech is called truth rather than mere narration?
premises: Non-distressing, true, pleasant-beneficial speech is called speech-born austerity.
Self-study and practice are also included.
Truth means determination of this very essential nature.
Pleasant-beneficial means pleasant at that time and beneficial at another time.
It is not mere narration of events.
inference: Truthful speech is defined by non-distress, present pleasantness, future benefit, and essential-nature determination, not by factual narration alone.
uncertainties: Whether self-study and practice are included within speech-born austerity or listed alongside it is not fully explicit.
The referent of "this very essential nature" in the truth-definition is not fully explicit.
plain_english: Speech that does not distress, is true, pleasant, and beneficial is called speech-born austerity, along with self-study and practice. "Truth" means determining this very essential nature; "pleasant and beneficial" means pleasant at that time and beneficial at another time. Such speech is called truth, not merely recounting events.
